summary: Comment-only cleanup is honest: parents and id are fresh named intermediates that are written once (per iteration for id) and hold the exact values in target registers $t0 (a0+0x94, stepped by 0x68) and $a3 (D_80094B9E, stepped by 0xA). Each is the only handle to its object. They read truthfully, so entry 6 / Ruling 1(3) needs no label. The comments' claims and the scores 3 / 5 were re-measured and are true. The body has no other codegen-only construct.

evidence.explanation: Written once before the loop. The target computes $t0 = a0+0x94 (= transform_nodes[1], since 0x2C+0x68) and stores it to parent_node each iteration, so the local names a real value only where the target already holds it. No other local or expression in the body reaches transform_nodes, so there is no extra handle. A programmer would plausibly write it this way: projected node i's parent is transform node i+1. Ablating it (in place, &arg0->transform_nodes[i + 1].node) gives sandbox score 3, which I re-measured and which matches the comment.

One assignment site per iteration, fresh, not borrowed. $a3 is exactly &recs[i].unk_08 (D_80094B96 recs + 8 = D_80094B9E, stride 0xA): it is loaded with lh, tested with beq against -1 and stored with sh at -0x56($a1), which is projected node +2 = unk2. The comment is true. The name id fits the header (unk_08 is the node's id, -1 = no node) and the sibling func_80040B44, which stores ids into unk2. Ablating it (read in place) gives sandbox score 5, re-measured, which matches the comment.

evidence.construct: rest of body (p walk over projected_nodes, field stores, terminator unk2 = -1)
evidence.explanation: No asm, pins, barriers, volatile or build changes. It uses the existing Unk80045878Obj / Unk80094B94Table types from game.h and the file, with no raw offsets or second extern. It has zero FAKE labels, so no lighter form is possible under item 5.
